changelog._extraSurfacesNote: There is no public/CHANGELOG.md here — the in-app data file is the only other surface. This check is deliberately REDUNDANT with the KNOWN_MISSING_FROM_MARKDOWN ratchet in the test suite, which asserts every version in changelogData.ts also appears in CHANGELOG.md. The ratchet is the stronger guard (it checks all 84 versions, not just the newest); this one fails faster and names the fix. Keep both.

extraSurfaces.note: In-app changelog. Sections use `title`, not `heading` — the landing page uses the other key.

_claudeMdNote: CLAUDE.md is gitignored, so the release checklist's consistency grep could never see version drift inside it — this file's 'Live facts' line claimed APP_VERSION 0.34.0 and 1159 tests across 74 files against an actual 0.34.2 / 1163 / 75. Only APP_VERSION is machine-checked; the test and file counts on the same line cannot be checked against package.json and must be updated by hand. Skipped in CI, where the file is never checked out. A second declaration, the `## Current State (vX.Y.Z)` heading, was found stale immediately after v0.34.4 shipped — the original pattern only matched the 'Live facts' line. Both are checked now; if another version declaration is added to CLAUDE.md, add its pattern here too.
_gitBaseBranchNote: Consumed by TWO scripts at two different moments, and the split is the point. shipgate.mjs uses it PRE-merge for one assertion only — that this clone is not BEHIND origin/<branch>, i.e. the release is being cut on top of current main. verify-sync.mjs uses it POST-merge for the three-way SHA comparison (local, remote-tracking, GitHub API) plus a clean-tree check. Neither check can live in the other's moment: the gate runs partway through a release with the version and changelog edits UNCOMMITTED, so a clean-tree assertion there would fail every release; and the post-merge SHA condition does not exist yet when the gate runs. Both self-skip under CI: actions/checkout is shallow and detached, so origin/<branch> is not a meaningful local ref there, and a CI runner has no view of a developer's clone at all — which is why this drift was invisible to every mechanism the suite already had. Remove this key to disable both checks; the gate then prints nothing for them rather than passing silently.

commands.name: lint
commands._note: eslint exits NON-ZERO here and that is correct — gate on the NUMBER not moving, never on the exit code. `expectProblems` is the single source of truth for the accepted baseline; it is deliberately the only place the count is written, so there is no second copy to go stale. Re-derive it from `npm run lint` immediately before each commit and set it in the same commit. All 13 are sonarjs/cognitive-complexity @ 15, all in production source, zero in test files — derived, not guessed, in the install commit (v0.35.0). William accepted this baseline from three measured options (14 narrow / 77 on sonarjs.configs.recommended / decline); do NOT refactor those functions merely to satisfy the threshold. The ratchet fails in BOTH directions — if problems are resolved, lower it. At true zero, DELETE this key: eslint emits no `✖ N problems` line and the gate would fail.

commands.name: typecheck
commands._note: Deliberately separate from `build`. `next build` typechecks the production build graph but NOT test files, so 33 type errors sat undetected in five __tests__ files — all of them Vitest 3→4 `vi.fn<Args, Return>` generics that silently typed the mocks as `never`, meaning those tests were not type-checking their own mock usage at all. Fixed in v0.34.4; this step is what keeps them fixed. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-17. This read: 'cfd and GanttApp were verified clean including tests, so they do not carry this step.' MEASURED: GanttApp has THREE errors (TS2802, es5 iteration without downlevelIteration, in two test files), introduced 2026-07-30 in c4e174a — THE SAME COMMIT THAT ADDED THE SHIP GATE — and green on every gate step continuously since. spert-cfd is genuinely clean, 0 errors verified 2026-08-17. So the claim was half true and wholly unfounded. ⚠️ It failed by CONSTRUCT VALIDITY, not by going stale: whoever 'verified clean including tests' ran a gate that cannot see test files, and got a truthful-looking green. Both states are true simultaneously and still are. THE RULE: a note asserting X must name the COMMAND that measured X. ⚠️ And cfd's cleanliness is not the gate's doing — it carries the identical exposure (Next.js, include **/*.ts, no typecheck script, no typecheck step) and is at zero by circumstance, helped by target ES2017 rather than es5. It can drift to GanttApp's state with nothing reporting it.
